question.text: Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) are registered under which SEBI regulation, and what is the minimum investment per investor?

explanation.text: The Logic: AIFs are registered under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 (not 2014). The general minimum investment per investor is Rs. 1 crore. A reduced Rs. 25 lakh minimum is available in specific situations - including for employees, directors and fund managers of the AIF, and per the Level 1 workbook (page 235) a limited number of AIFs offer accredited investors a Rs. 25 lakh ticket size instead of Rs. 1 crore. The Trap: 2014 is a common trap because REITs and InvITs were introduced in 2014 and candidates may incorrectly apply the same year to AIFs. AIFs came earlier, in 2012. Rs. 25 lakhs is not the general investor minimum - it is a narrow exception, not the headline rule. Note: The Rs. 1 crore minimum keeps AIFs largely confined to HNI / ultra-HNI clients. Where a Rs. 25 lakh minimum is offered, it is restricted either to fund insiders (employees / directors / managers) or to accredited investors in the few AIFs that have adopted that ticket size.
